finding.summary: get_commits_between() returns data['commits'] from a single compare response and build_incremental_diff() returns resp.text with no truncation check. GitHub's compare endpoint returns at most 250 commits and truncates large diffs, so for a large --since-last-review increment the agent can review a partial diff, post it as a complete REVIEW_SIGNATURE report, and record head_sha as the new baseline. The un-reviewed commits are then permanently skipped on subsequent runs — exactly the false all-clear this PR's fail-loudly redesign is meant to prevent.
finding.fix: Detect truncation before trusting the increment: compare len(data['commits']) against data.get('total_commits') (and/or fetch the compare JSON first and check its 'truncated' flag before requesting the .diff media type). When truncated, print a warning and fall back to a full review instead of building an incremental diff.
